title: Different Breeds of Dairy Cattle:
text:
Different Breeds of Dairy Cattle:

BREEDS | CHARACTERISTICS

GUERNSEY
Origin: Isle of Guernsey, France
Markings: Yellow to reddish-brown & white
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Very efficient converters
✓ Adaptable to different management systems
✓ Heat tolerance
✓ Docile temperament
✓ Calving ease
Performance:
✓ 500-700kg
✓ 6000kg/lactation (305days)
✓ Fat: 4.7%
✓ Protein: 3.4%

DAIRY SHORTHORN
Origin: Great Britain
Purpose: Milk & beef
Markings: White & roan
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ High protein-to-fat ratio
✓ Quiet temperament
✓ Efficient converter
✓ Strong legs and improved longevity
Performance:
✓ 640-680kg
✓ 7000kg/lactation
✓ Fat: 4.0%
✓ Protein: 3.5%

ARYSHIRE
Origin: County of Ayr, Scotland
Markings: Red & white, brindle & roan (rare)
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Efficient converter
✓ Strong legs & excellent udder conformation
✓ Vigorous calves
✓ Free from genetic disease
Performance:
✓ 450-600kg
✓ 7700kg/lactation
✓ Fat: 3.9%
✓ Protein: 3.3%

facts: The Guernsey breed originates from Isle of Guernsey, France.
Guernsey cattle markings are yellow to reddish-brown and white.
Desirable characteristics of Guernsey include: very efficient converters, adaptable to different management systems, heat tolerance, docile temperament, and calving ease.
Performance specifications of Guernsey: weight is 500-700 kg, milk yield is 6000 kg/lactation (305 days), fat content is 4.7%, and protein content is 3.4%.
Dairy Shorthorn originates from Great Britain.
Dairy Shorthorn is dual-purpose: used for both milk and beef.
Dairy Shorthorn markings are white and roan.
Desirable characteristics of Dairy Shorthorn include: high protein-to-fat ratio, quiet temperament, efficient converter, strong legs, and improved longevity.
Performance specifications of Dairy Shorthorn: weight is 640-680 kg, milk yield is 7000 kg/lactation, fat content is 4.0%, and protein content is 3.5%.
Ayrshire (spelled ARYSHIRE on page) originates from County of Ayr, Scotland.
Ayrshire markings are red & white, with brindle & roan being rare.
Desirable characteristics of Ayrshire include: efficient converter, strong legs & excellent udder conformation, vigorous calves, and free from genetic disease.
Performance specifications of Ayrshire: weight is 450-600 kg, milk yield is 7700 kg/lactation, fat content is 3.9%, and protein content is 3.3%.
